clarifications.decision: The future retained I/O session owns descriptors, edges, stamps and final verification. The first foundation increment only selects an origin plan and compiles an exact immutable byte collection into a structural resource view. It performs no resource file opens or cleanup and cannot establish lineage authority by itself.
Exactly ten schema IDs are registry resources. The profile is validated by the common schema /$defs/profile fragment; there is no eleventh schema resource or profile ID registration.

R8 governs: names/set checks surround each write, while full byte rereads occur at its bounded acquisition/publication/cleanup/fsync/final checkpoints. Do not demand a full reread of all resources after every one-byte short write.

A valid resealed semantic forgery may pass structural validation. Foundation APIs must label that result structural only and cannot expose accepted/eligible/public-command success. The later public layer must reject the forgery through identity/reference/derived replay as applicable.

The foundation reports fixed private resource reasons without exposing raw paths/parser/resolver data. The I/O boundary builds the full nine-field R8 context and retains missing/unsafe input reasons where contracted. Every final retained lineage failure takes R8 precedence; do not replace the R8 context with a smaller reason-only public error.

remaining_before_dispatch: Concrete private API/source/test allowlist and reviewed instruction-only packet
Freeze any introduced primitive bounds explicitly; metadata depth/integer-range limits are not inferred from jcs.py, which accepts arbitrary Python integers.
